title: Lung anatomy: lobes, bronchi and alveoli
description: Two elastic, pleura-lined organs where air and blood come within 0.5 µm of each other.

questions.question: How does oxygen get from the lungs into the blood?
questions.answer: Air reaches the alveoli through branching airways. Oxygen diffuses across the thin alveolar-capillary barrier into pulmonary capillaries, while carbon dioxide moves in the opposite direction.

questions.question: Why does the right lung have three lobes and the left have two?
questions.answer: The right lung is divided into upper, middle and lower lobes. The left has upper and lower lobes and a cardiac notch that accommodates the heart.

questions.question: What are the bronchioles?
questions.answer: Airways under 1 mm with no cartilage and relatively more smooth muscle, ending in terminal then respiratory bronchioles. Function: Regulate airflow resistance and deliver air to the alveolar ducts.

questions.question: Where is the pleura & pleural cavity located?
questions.answer: Visceral pleura covers the lung; parietal pleura lines the wall. Between them is a potential space with a film of serous fluid. Function: Surface tension couples the lung to the chest wall so it expands with it, and the fluid lets the layers glide.

questions.question: What is the function of the alveoli & capillary bed?
questions.answer: Function: Diffusion of O₂ into blood and CO₂ out of it. Thin-walled sacs of type I pneumocytes wrapped in capillaries; type II pneumocytes secrete surfactant and alveolar macrophages patrol the surface. Together they present ~70 m² of membrane only 0.5 µm thick.
